subject: biology
title: Continuous and Discontinuous
welcome_lead: Spot the difference between features on a sliding scale and features that fall into clear groups.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on continuous and discontinuous variation.
final_note: You can now tell continuous from discontinuous variation with everyday examples.

concepts.def: Variation with a range of values.

walkthroughs.body_html: Continuous variation has a smooth range of values, like height or weight. It is shown best on a line graph or histogram.
Discontinuous variation has clear separate categories, like blood group (A, B, AB, O) or whether earlobes are attached. Shown on a bar chart.
Continuous: height, hand span, shoe size, foot length. Discontinuous: eye colour, blood group, whether you can roll your tongue, gender at birth.

mcqs.q: Discontinuous variation is shown best with…
What distinguishes the innate from the adaptive immune response?
options: Innate is fast, non-specific, and has no memory; adaptive is slower initially, highly specific, and forms memory cells.
Innate immunity only works in children; adaptive only works in adults.
Innate immunity attacks viruses and adaptive attacks bacteria.
Missense and silent mutations always produce a non-functional protein.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a silent and a missense mutation?
options: A silent mutation changes a base but the codon still codes for the same amino acid; a missense mutation changes the amino acid encoded.
Innate immunity only works in children; adaptive only works in adults.
A silent mutation has no effect because no base actually changes.
Missense and silent mutations always produce a non-functional protein.

mcqs.q: Why is the cohesion-tension theory critical for water transport in plants?
options: Cohesion-tension explains how plants store water in the xylem like a reservoir.
Missense and silent mutations always produce a non-functional protein.
Cohesion-tension describes how water diffuses freely between cells.
Hydrogen bonds between water molecules keep the water column unbroken under tension, so transpiration can pull water up from the roots.
